newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-MATCHES IN ITALY SERIE A.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-MATCHES IN ITALY SERIE A.

text.p: Italian Serie A games scheduled for Sunday (standings in parentheses, kickoff times GMT):
In-form Bologna complete with Swede Kennet Andersson and Russian Igor Kolivanov should be too strong for second from bottom Verona, notwithstanding their 3-1 win against AC Milan last week.

Seems like mission impossible for struggling Cagliari who will field a 5-4-1 formation with only Sandro Tovalieri in attack in the hope of holding out against a Juventus side led by strikers Alessandro Del Piero and Michele Padovano in the continued absence of injured Croat striker Alen Boksic.

Unbeaten in eight games since November 24th, Atalanta could prove an awkward customer for Fiorentina, led by Argentine Gabriel Batistuta and Brazilian Oliveira in attack. Fiorentina's $12 million midweek purchase, Russian Andrei Kanchelskis from English club Everton, will make his club debut in two weeks time against Verona.

Following a 3-1 defeat by Verona last week, Milan coach Arrigo Sacchi will hope that the return of Liberian striker George Weah can refloat his side's miserable season. Sampdoria with 16 points from their last six outings field their terrible twin strike force of captain Roberto Mancini and Vincenzo Montella, combined scorers of 24 goals.

Piacenza have not won since beating AC Milan 3-2 at home on December 1 while they have not won an away game for 21 months and look unlikely to improve on that record in this derby clash. Parma, with Enrico Chiesa and Argentine Hernan Crespo in attack, should be too strong, notwithstanding a 2-1 defeat by Napoli last Sunday.

Perugia "old boy" Fabrizio Ravanelli, now with English side Middlesborough, turned up for a mid-week training session with his former club who, with just three points in their last eight games, need all the help they can get. Croat Milan Rapajic and Marco Negri lead the Perugia attack with new signing Brazlian Muller on standby. Inter, held to a midweek 1-1 Italian Cup semifinal first leg draw by Napoli, look to Frenchman Youri Djorkaeff, Maurizio Ganz and Chilean Ivan Zamorano for better things.

Bottom club Reggiana look to strikers Russian Igor Simutenkov and Colombian Freddy Valencia against a bouyant Napoli authoritatively led by Brazilian libero-cum-midfielder Andre Cruz. Reggiana are unlikely to halt their seemingly inevitable slide back into division two.

Both Rome clubs, AS Roma and Lazio, are in crisis. Held to a 0-0 away draw by Piacenza on Sunday, Roma hope to improve things by introducing two recent purchases, French midfielder Vincent Candela, ex-Guingamp, and Russian defender Omari Tetradze, ex-Alanija Vladikavkaz. Vicenza, 3-2 winners against Fiorentina on Sunday, may spoil the debuts.

Lazio 's current poor form led to the midweek sacking of Czech coach Zdenek Zeman, replaced by club president and '82 World Cup winning captain Dino Zoff. The new coach may be more cautious than his predecessor and field a 4-4-2 line-up with midfielder Giorgio Venturin coming in for striker Roberto Rambaudi. Udinese, without three injured foreigners in German striker Oliver Bierhoff, Egyptian midfielder Emam Hazem and Polish defender Marek Kozminski, rely on Paolo Poggi and Brazilian Amoroso in attack.
